governanceNotes: D1 batch 69 (2026-09-26): two bounded association edges authored - patent-ductus-arteriosus to pulmonary-hypertension (rank 1) and to congestive-heart-failure (rank 2) - both classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true, mechanismCategory THROMBOTIC_OR_VASCULAR consistent with the atrial-septal-defect shunt-to-pulmonary-hypertension precedent. The pulmonary-hypertension edge rests on the shunt-pathophysiology overview with Eisenmenger framing (PMID 42661256), the adult closure-registry review (PMID 42525314), and the isolated-PDA severe-PHT case (PMID 41362902); the heart-failure edge rests on the edema and closure-improvement framing (PMIDs 42661256, 42711802) and the adult preterm remodeling cohort (PMID 41986666).

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-26: (i) prematurity shared substrate - bronchopulmonary dysplasia and prematurity lung disease co-drive pulmonary hypertension in the preterm populations where PDA is common, and prematurity programming drives adult blood pressure and myocardial development; the edges are scoped with these confounds carried openly; (ii) partially definitional exposure - the adult cohort defined symptomatic PDA partly by congestive heart failure at presentation, so the heart-failure edge's basis carries this circularity openly and leans on the review anchors for the pathway; (iii) withheld propositions with no catalog identities - bronchopulmonary dysplasia, necrotizing enterocolitis, and infective endocarditis (the PDA association literature is correlation-level or case-class; evidence preserved here); (iv) ME-29 - the atrial-septal-defect pulmonary-hypertension window and the myocarditis/cardiomyopathy windows are not recycled; all anchors are PDA-specific sources.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Patent ductus arteriosus documents pulmonary hypertension at review and registry level: the Cardiology Review PDA overview describes the left-to-right shunt manifesting with pulmonary hypertension symptoms and progressing to reversed shunt (Eisenmenger syndrome) when untreated (PMID 42661256), the multicenter adult transcatheter-closure registry review reports pulmonary arterial hypertension commonly present in adults with PDA complicating clinical decision-making (PMID 42525314), and the preterm isolated-PDA case with severe pulmonary hypertension and lung-biopsy-confirmed pulmonary interstitial glycogenosis documents the pathway's severe end (PMID 41362902); recorded as documented association only with the preterm and adult scope split carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the anchors are narrative reviews, a registry overview, and a single case, no primary cohort quantifies incident pulmonary hypertension after PDA, prematurity and bronchopulmonary dysplasia co-drive pulmonary hypertension in the preterm population, and individual claims require dated echocardiography with prematurity-lung-disease, thromboembolic, and left-heart-disease exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Chronic left-to-right ductal shunting increases pulmonary blood flow and drives pulmonary vascular remodeling so pulmonary arterial hypertension results, the flow-overload route supported by the documented Eisenmenger progression and by pulmonary arterial hypertension commonly complicating adult PDA management, but whether this route produced any individual pulmonary hypertension remains hypothesized until echocardiographic and catheterization records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at narrative-review plus registry-overview plus single-case class only: no primary cohort quantifies pulmonary-hypertension incidence in PDA, the preterm evidence is confounded by bronchopulmonary dysplasia and prematurity lung disease (the PDA-BPD literature frames them as co-driven rather than causal), and adult PDA cohorts are referral-selected toward shunts surviving to closure.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No primary cohort quantifies incident pulmonary hypertension after PDA; the preterm literature is confounded by bronchopulmonary dysplasia and prematurity lung disease with PDA-BPD correlation rather than attribution; the severe-PHT case (PMID 41362902) is a single report with a lung-biopsy confound; adult registry data are referral-selected; and prematurity lung disease, thromboembolic disease, left-heart disease, and connective-tissue disease compete for individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: bronchopulmonary dysplasia and prematurity lung disease (shared driver in preterm populations)
connective-tissue-disease pulmonary arterial hypertension (published windows, not recycled per ME-29)

evidenceGaps: No primary cohort quantifies incident pulmonary hypertension after PDA; the preterm literature is confounded by bronchopulmonary dysplasia and prematurity lung disease with PDA-BPD correlation rather than attribution; the severe-PHT case (PMID 41362902) is a single report with a lung-biopsy confound; adult registry data are referral-selected; and prematurity lung disease, thromboembolic disease, left-heart disease, and connective-tissue disease compete for individual attribution.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at review plus registry class with the preterm-confound and incidence-gap limits carried openly: the Cardiology Review overview frames the ductal shunt as manifesting with pulmonary hypertension symptoms and Eisenmenger progression (PMID 42661256), the adult closure-registry review reports pulmonary arterial hypertension commonly complicating adult PDA management (PMID 42525314), and the isolated-PDA severe-PHT case documents the pathway's extreme (PMID 41362902); because no primary incidence cohort exists and preterm populations share the bronchopulmonary-dysplasia driver, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through dated echocardiography with prematurity-lung-disease, thromboembolic, and left-heart exclusion.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Patent ductus arteriosus documents heart-failure physiology at review and cohort level: the Cardiology Review PDA overview describes the left-to-right shunt manifesting with pulmonary-hypertension symptoms and edema (PMID 42661256), the adult PDA management review reports closure producing considerable hemodynamic and clinical improvement (PMID 42711802), and the 107-person young-adult preterm cohort defined symptomatic PDA in infancy by large left-to-right shunt or congestive heart failure and found those with symptomatic PDA carried higher resting diastolic pressure, lower tissue-Doppler diastolic velocities, and larger right ventricular dimensions in early adulthood (PMID 41986666); recorded as documented association only with the partially definitional exposure and subclinical-outcome limits carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the cohort's symptomatic-PDA exposure definition includes congestive heart failure (partially definitional), the adult-outcome differences are subclinical remodeling rather than heart-failure diagnoses, and individual claims require dated echocardiography and clinical assessment with ischemic, valvular, and myocardial exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Chronic left-to-right ductal shunting imposes volume overload on the left heart and pulmonary circulation so high-output heart failure with edema results, the overload route supported by hemodynamic improvement after closure and by persistent diastolic and right-ventricular remodeling in adults who had symptomatic PDA, but whether this route produced any individual heart failure remains hypothesized until echocardiographic and clinical records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at narrative-review plus retrospective-cohort class only: the defining cohort exposure includes congestive heart failure at presentation (partially definitional), the adult findings are subclinical remodeling differences at group level without heart-failure diagnoses, prematurity co-drives myocardial development, and no untreated comparison exists.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The review anchors are narrative class; the defining cohort exposure includes congestive heart failure at presentation (partially definitional); the adult follow-up differences are subclinical remodeling without clinical heart-failure outcomes; prematurity itself alters myocardial development (shared substrate in the adult cohort); and ischemic, valvular, and myocardial diseases compete for individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: prematurity-related myocardial development differences (shared driver in the adult preterm cohort)
myocarditis and cardiomyopathy (published windows, not recycled per ME-29)
right-heart failure downstream of pulmonary hypertension (the parallel PDA pulmonary-hypertension pathway in this file)

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at review plus cohort class with the definitional-exposure and subclinical-outcome limits carried openly: the review anchors frame the ductal shunt with edema and hemodynamic improvement after closure (PMIDs 42661256, 42711802), and the adult preterm cohort documents persistent diastolic and right-ventricular remodeling after symptomatic PDA in infancy (PMID 41986666); because the cohort exposure definition includes congestive heart failure and the adult differences are subclinical, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through dated echocardiography with ischemic, valvular, myocardial, and renal exclusion.
